requirement: Stop a PyTorch training loop when validation loss stops improving and keep a copy of the best weights to restore afterwards.
skeleton: An EarlyStopping class validating patience and min_delta, tracking best loss, a deep-copied best state and bad epochs, with step returning whether to stop.
caption: A PyTorch-style early stopping helper, written in the standard library against a duck-typed model with a state_dict method and no third-party imports. EarlyStopping(patience=5, min_delta=0.0) raises ValueError when patience is below 1 or min_delta is negative, and starts with best_loss at math.inf, best_state None and zero bad epochs. step(val_loss, model) raises ValueError for a NaN loss. When the loss is below best_loss minus min_delta it records the loss, stores copy.deepcopy of model.state_dict(), resets the bad epoch count and returns False; otherwise it counts a bad epoch and returns True once the count reaches patience. The fixture asserts counter resets and snapshots, that the snapshot is a deep copy, stopping after exactly patience bad epochs, min_delta, that any first loss improves, NaN rejection, and argument validation.

plan.intent: Avoid overfitting by stopping training at the best epoch
constraints: patience below 1 or negative min_delta raises ValueError
A NaN validation loss raises ValueError
Improvement must beat best_loss by more than min_delta
The best state_dict is deep copied
Training stops when bad epochs reach patience

rationale.teaches: Compare against best minus min_delta, snapshot state_dict with deepcopy so later optimizer steps cannot mutate it, and reset the counter on every improvement.
rationale.why: state_dict returns live tensors, so a shallow snapshot silently tracks the latest weights and restoring it restores nothing; off-by-one patience trains an extra epoch.

ops.docstring: Early stopping that snapshots the best model state_dict, torch-style.

candidates.why_wrong: A shallow copy shares nested weights, so the snapshot follows later updates.
Tiny improvements below min_delta still reset the patience counter.
Bad epochs are not reset on improvement, so training stops too early.
Training stops one epoch after the patience limit is reached.
A first loss above a million is not treated as an improvement.
